xBRIEFInfo.description: Plan for PAN-4628: npx launch: panes get a stale internal token, so pan pair and other CLI calls are rejected

plan.title: npx launch: panes get a stale internal token, so pan pair and other CLI calls are rejected
plan.author: agent:claude-opus-5-5

narratives.Problem: pan serve (the npx @overdeck/core launcher, src/cli/index.ts lines 1215-1272) mints a throwaway internal token per run and passes it to the dashboard only through OVERDECK_INTERNAL_TOKEN in env; it never writes <OVERDECK_HOME>/internal-token. Every token reader prefers env over the file. A long-lived Herdr server spawned from that dashboard captures the env token, and every pane inherits it; after the next npx launch the dashboard holds a new token, so pan pair, pan devices, other CLI senders and hook heartbeats from panes get 401/403. On a fresh npx machine pan pair fails too: with no file, a CLI generates a new file token the env-only server never saw.
narratives.Proposal: Make the token file the single source of truth (PRD D-1..D-4). All seven readers resolve file -> env -> none: getInternalToken/ensureInternalToken in src/lib/internal-token.ts, readInternalTokenForRequest in routes/agents/shared.ts, the caveman hook script, and the four shell hooks. ensureInternalToken seeds a missing file from env (or a random token) with mode 0600, and caches by source so request paths do no file I/O after boot. pan serve is extracted to src/cli/commands/serve.ts, resolves its token with ensureInternalToken, and stops adding the token to the server child's env. pan pair's 401 message explains a token mismatch and the restart remedy. DASHBOARD-AUTH.md and remote-access.mdx document the file-first order.
narratives.NonGoals:
- Injecting the internal token into pane env, or any change to launchAgentPane or src/lib/terminal-backends/*
- Stripping OVERDECK_INTERNAL_TOKEN from the Herdr server's spawn env, or restarting Herdr
- A pan doctor env-vs-file check, or a boot warning when an env token is ignored
- Rotating the internal token, or retry-on-401 logic in CLI senders
- Changing pan serve's description or --port option (no skill file changes)
- Raising any scripts/file-size-allowlist.txt row
- pan connect (PAN-4656, W-LINK9), machine links, Tailscale, the directory, trusted-origins changes, and every other PAN-2350 work item owned by a sibling issue

autoDecisions.summary: Fix stale panes by making every token reader file-first, not by injecting the current token into pane env at launch
autoDecisions.rationale: File-first repairs panes that already exist (each pan call and hook run re-resolves), also works when launchAgentPane runs in a CLI process that holds a stale env value, and keeps the root secret out of agent environments and transcripts (remote-access.mdx: the root token never leaves the machine). Injection would only reach panes launched after the fix.

autoDecisions.summary: ensureInternalToken seeds a missing token file from OVERDECK_INTERNAL_TOKEN (else a random token)
autoDecisions.rationale: After the first ensure on a home the file always exists, so every reader agrees; the Windows smoke probe (env token, fresh home) keeps working because its env value becomes the file value.

autoDecisions.summary: Extract the pan serve action to src/cli/commands/serve.ts with injectable spawn and browser opener
autoDecisions.rationale: Makes the token and child-env behavior unit-testable, follows the existing lazyAction command pattern, and shrinks the src/cli/index.ts god file instead of growing it.

autoDecisions.summary: Override the issue's 'Docs: None' and update docs/DASHBOARD-AUTH.md and configuration/remote-access.mdx
autoDecisions.rationale: remote-access.mdx lines 85-87 state that pan pair needs a pan up dashboard, which this issue makes false; DASHBOARD-AUTH.md describes the token without its resolution order.

metadata.sizeJustification: Seven small items across src/lib, the dashboard auth reader, CLI commands, shell hooks and two docs; all encode one token-resolution contract and are under the file and subsystem limits.

items.title: Resolve the internal token file-first in src/lib/internal-token.ts

verify_commands: npx vitest run $(grep -rlE "internal-token\.js'|OVERDECK_INTERNAL_TOKEN" src tests --include=*.test.ts | grep -v src/dashboard/frontend)
expected_outputs: internal-token.test.ts passes, including 'file wins over a stale env token' and 'env seeds the file when none exists'
every non-frontend test file that imports the internal-token module or sets OVERDECK_INTERNAL_TOKEN exits 0 under vitest

narrative.Action: Implement PRD work item 1 exactly: replace the module cache with a source-tracked cache ({token, source: 'file'|'env'} | null); add readTokenFile() and envToken() helpers; getInternalToken() returns file (non-empty) else env else null and never writes; ensureInternalToken() returns a file-sourced cache without I/O, else reads the file, else writes envToken() ?? randomBytes(32).toString('hex') to <OVERDECK_HOME>/internal-token with mode 0600 (keep the existing mkdir 0700 and best-effort chmodSync) and caches it as source 'file'. _resetInternalTokenCacheForTests() resets the new cache. Rewrite the module header to state the file-first order and the PAN-4628 reason. Add src/lib/__tests__/internal-token.test.ts with the four cases named in the PRD; each beforeEach resets the cache and removes the token file and OVERDECK_INTERNAL_TOKEN. Then run the regression sweep over every test file importing the module; if one breaks because the seed write leaves a file behind, fix that test by deleting the token file in its beforeEach, never by changing the resolver. The sweep command uses shell expansion; if the slot runner does not run it through a shell, expand the file list by hand with the same grep.

narrative.Action: Implement PRD work item 5: move the serve action body from src/cli/index.ts (lines 1215-1272) into export async function serveCommand(options: { port: string }, deps: ServeDeps = {}) in new src/cli/commands/serve.ts, with injectable spawn, openBrowser and openDelayMs (default 1500). Resolve the bundle as join(packageRoot, 'dist', 'dashboard', 'server.js') and join(packageRoot, 'dist', 'dashboard', 'public', 'index.html') using packageRoot from src/lib/paths.ts, never import.meta.url (lazy dist chunks, PAN-4195). After the bundle check, const internalToken = ensureInternalToken(); spawn the server with env { ...process.env, PORT: String(port) } (no OVERDECK_INTERNAL_TOKEN key added). Keep messages, exit paths and the browser fallback line. In index.ts keep the comment and command registration and use .action(lazyAction(() => import('./commands/serve.js'), 'serveCommand')). Write tests/unit/cli/serve.test.ts with fake timers (vi.useFakeTimers + vi.advanceTimersByTimeAsync), a fake spawn and opener, and packageRoot mocked to a temp dir holding empty bundle files. Then run the PRD's implementation checkpoint (build, isolated serve on a free port with OVERDECK_TERMINAL_BACKEND=tmux, OVERDECK_DISABLE_DEACON=1, OVERDECK_DISABLE_AUTO_MERGE=1, then pan pair --url http://192.0.2.10:<port> --json with a stale env token); kill the server by its literal PID. If the live run is impossible, record why in the PR body. Mock packageRoot with a partial vi.mock using importOriginal: internal-token.ts imports getOverdeckHome from the same paths module, so a full mock breaks it.
